House Chores Checklist

Running a household is a rolling list of jobs on different clocks — some daily, some weekly, a few only monthly. Written down and split by frequency, that invisible workload becomes something you can plan around and share fairly between everyone in the home. This checklist gathers the recurring chores in one place so nothing slips until it becomes a bigger job. See more cleaning and chore checklists.

Frequently asked questions

How do I split house chores fairly? expand_more

Start by writing every recurring job down and how often it needs doing, then divide by time and effort rather than by task count — one big weekly job can equal several small daily ones. A shared checklist everyone can see keeps it transparent and stops the same person always doing the invisible work.

What chores should be done weekly? expand_more

The weekly core is changing bed sheets, vacuuming and mopping all floors, cleaning the bathroom top to bottom, dusting surfaces, wiping kitchen appliances, doing the laundry, and emptying the bins. Keeping up with daily tidying makes these go much faster.

How often should you do each household chore? expand_more

Dishes, surfaces, and tidying are daily. Sheets, floors, the bathroom, dusting, and laundry are weekly. Deeper jobs — the oven, descaling, windows, under the furniture, and washing-machine maintenance — are monthly. Splitting chores this way keeps any single job from becoming a big one.
